challenge.heading: When budget decisions are driven by legacy and organisation in place
challenge.body:
A global biopharmaceutical company operating across multiple therapeutic areas was investing heavily across sales force, digital and events — but had no reliable way to know which channels were actually driving impact. Budget decisions were made on historical precedent and organisational design rather than evidence. Senior leaders disagreed on the value of the different channels, yet most continued to be funded at similar levels with little data to arbitrate.

As the organisation moved towards omnichannel engagement, attribution became harder. Field teams were overcalling certain HCP segments, underfunding high-potential accounts, and Marketing was deploying digital channels with no plans to measure return. Each annual planning cycle reopened the same unresolved debate: where should we invest to deliver our ambition?

What was missing was not ambition or investment — it was the analytical infrastructure to connect commercial spend to commercial outcomes, and a shared language for leaders to make resource decisions with confidence.

approach.heading: Building the analytical engine behind smarter commercial decisions

items.title: Commercial Excellence Foundation
items.description: Before modelling, we put in place a structured health check approach of commercial excellence fundamentals — segmentation and targeting, Account Planning and execution, call plan coverage, channel mix allocation analysis. Descriptive analytics established a clear baseline of what was actually happening across the promotional mix, surfacing significant gaps between intended strategy and actual execution, and building leadership credibility for the analytical work that followed.

items.title: Marketing Mix Modelling
items.description: We deployed a multi-channel attribution model that decomposed sales into their constituent drivers: field force detailing, meetings and events, digital engagement, seasonality, and competitor activity. The model revealed various patterns depending on the analysed brand, with sometimes a significant mismatch between where budget was concentrated and where sales were actually being generated.

items.title: Response Curves & ROI Analysis
items.description: For each channel, we built response curves mapping the relationship between investment and incremental sales — distinguishing marginal ROI from average ROI. This identified frequency thresholds beyond which detailing or activity generated diminishing returns, exposed underfunded channels with significant headroom, and shifted leadership thinking from how much did we spend to what did the last dollar of investment actually return.

items.title: Capability Building
items.description: The most durable outcome was the change in how decisions were made. We co-developed an interactive scenario planning tool with brand teams, enabling them to simulate allocation decisions independently. Structured capability sessions reframed the annual budgeting conversation — from a negotiation anchored in last year's spend to an evidence-based dialogue about marginal impact. Senior leaders described it as the first time they felt genuinely equipped to make confident investment decisions.
